text: The full Playwright suite intermittently redirected the existing Google-account sign-in test to the demo repertoire; an isolated three-run repeat and the next full run passed, so the auth redirect race needs deterministic synchronization.

The frontend manually revalidates trusted /api/games responses field-by-field, duplicating backend contracts and making additive or rolling API changes fail as 'invalid-response'. Prefer a generated/versioned API client or typed DTO boundary, and avoid client validation of server-owned invariants such as result limits.

Full Playwright run stalled five unrelated workers simultaneously for about 2.5 minutes; the same five tests passed immediately with --workers=1. A documented/resource-aware local worker setting would prevent false timeout failures.
Full parallel E2E can remove the automatic training move animation before animationstart fires; the fixed 270ms cleanup races a delayed first paint.
Visual browser verification on port 5174 blocked the subsequent Playwright run; stop the preview server before starting E2E.

The learning E2E asserts a 400ms transient moving-piece element after a separate text assertion, so it can miss the animation under parallel worker load; record animationstart before navigation instead.
tsx runs TypeScript scripts as CommonJS here, so top-level await fails; a documented script entry-point convention would prevent this

The training queue E2E expected Read line to be disabled even though the component and route already provide a valid href; keeping route-action assertions aligned would avoid unrelated focused-test failures
Playwright could not start because localhost:5174 was already occupied; a pre-test port check or cleanup would prevent the failed run.
gh pr edit fails on this repository because it queries deprecated Projects classic projectCards; using the pull-request REST API avoids the unrelated GraphQL failure
@better-auth/electron 1.7.2 client plugin types are incompatible with exactOptionalPropertyTypes, forcing an Electron-only compiler override

Full frontend check produced two transient repertoire learning/training E2E failures that passed immediately in isolation; stabilize animation/event timing so unrelated changes can trust the full suite.

Sandboxed Electron preload silently failed because the multi-entry Vite build split shared IPC constants into a relative chunk; keep the preload self-contained and retain an E2E assertion that the real preload bridge reaches shell.openExternal.

Electron auth E2E covered opening the browser but not the post-OAuth broker handoff, allowing the global auth handler to consume desktop auth_event before the broker. Keep an E2E callback-cookie-to-deep-link test.

Desktop auth broker E2E seeded the authorization cookie before mount, bypassing the real delayed-cookie polling path and missing a Solid cleanup-scope crash. Seed it after navigation and inspect live browser console errors.

The full Playwright suite consistently fails three unrelated repertoire tests: stable evaluation preview never renders data-evaluation-depth=20; black repertoire learning records no first move after the board intro; and locked training input lets the e7 pawn move before the response. Investigate shared animation/engine readiness and event-ordering assumptions so npm run check is reliable.

Full frontend check intermittently missed the white-learning move animation event under suite load; the focused test passed immediately, so the event-sequence assertion needs deterministic synchronization.
Shell commands targeting bracket-named route files fail under zsh unless every path is quoted; examples or a wrapper would prevent this.
Sandbox prevents npm registry access, localhost test listeners and CoreSimulator; run dependency installs and integration checks with approved escalation.
Native iOS build needs CocoaPods 1.16 or newer; old pod rejects visionos in current RN podspecs. Add a prerequisite check before expo run:ios.
Full unit suite cannot bind the desktop auth loopback callback under the sandbox (listen EPERM on 127.0.0.1); allow the test's local callback listener during verification.
npm registry lookups stall under the restricted network sandbox; request network access for npm metadata and installation and use short fetch timeouts for lookups.

The full check stops on pre-existing formatting in apps/native/tests/api.test.ts before testing the Solid upgrade; keeping the baseline formatted would allow dependency upgrades to use the standard check command.
The desktop auth unit test and browser test runner need localhost listeners, which the sandbox denies with EPERM; run the repository verification with localhost permission.
Repository-wide format check is blocked by existing formatting in apps/native/tests/api.test.ts; keeping committed files formatter-clean would let unrelated feature checks pass.
Desktop auth unit test cannot bind its loopback callback port under the sandbox (listen EPERM on 127.0.0.1); running that test with local-port permission avoids an unrelated full-suite failure.
The optional boolean prop guardrail was only discovered during checks; documenting it in AGENTS.md would prevent rework.
Running the repository formatter changed unrelated existing formatting in apps/native/tests/api.test.ts. A clean baseline format check would avoid unrelated diffs during scoped feature work.
The full unit suite's desktop auth loopback test failed with listen EPERM under the sandbox. Declaring its localhost-listener permission requirement would prevent an avoidable failed full-suite run.
Local browser tests require unsandboxed loopback binding; use the approved npm test command with escalation instead of retrying a blocked server launch.

The iOS test destination hard-coded an older phone model with OS=latest, which no longer existed after an Xcode runtime update. Select an available simulator by ID and keep the explicit destination override.
The generated native UI test target omitted PRODUCT_NAME, causing Xcode 27 to produce duplicate empty .xctest output paths. Set its product name explicitly in the test-project generator.
Full npm run check reached browser tests but the sandbox denied binding localhost (::1, EPERM). Browser checks need permission to open the local test server; distinguish this from a failing test.
Browser regression tests could not bind localhost inside the sandbox (listen EPERM on ::1); allowing local test-server ports would avoid an extra approval step.
Fetch mocks typed as typeof fetch unexpectedly require Bun's preconnect property; use a function signature based on Parameters/ReturnType so browser API tests do not inherit runtime-specific statics.

Solid component tests need explicit cleanup between cases; an undisposed earlier view consumed the next test's one-shot mock after a shared game-change notification. Add afterEach(cleanup) to multi-case component tests.
The full browser test runner was blocked by sandbox listen EPERM on ::1 after focused runs worked; localhost server permissions should be available consistently for repository checks.
